verses.1: When it was decided that we should go to Italy, Paul and some other believers were given orders to be led by Julius, a centurion.
verses.2: When we arrived at the ship of Adramyttus, which was about to sail to the places in Asia, we were accompanied by our commander Aristarchus from Macedon, Thessalonica.
verses.3: We also heard from him in Sidoine. He was a kind-hearted man; he allowed those who were being sent away to be taken care of with attention and care.
verses.4: From there, we continued our journey towards Cyprus, because the winds blew in opposite directions.
verses.5: Then, after crossing the sea along the coast of Kilikia and Pamphylia, we arrived at Mura in Lycia.
verses.6: There, the centurion found a ship from Alexandria, which was then transported to Italy. We were brought there using that ship.
verses.7: In those days, we traveled through the darkness of the night, and we only appeared on the coast of Knidon. Without being seen by the wind, we crossed Crete along the coast of Salmone.
verses.8: Once we reached that place, which was called Kalos Limena, there was a city named Lasia.
verses.9: When it was time for the ship to be sailed again, and since the ship was already ready to set sail, due to the fact that the fasting period had already been completed, Paul arrived.
verses.10: I say to them: Men, I believe that not only will we be burdened with taxes and many other penalties, but our souls will also be affected negatively by this situation.
verses.11: But the centurion was more feared by the governor and the naval commander than those who were called “Pavlus’s followers”.
verses.12: Since there was no clear path through the harbor, those who had more resources decided to move there instead. They hoped that they could get into Phoinikia by crossing over to the shores of Crete, both from a nautical and geographical perspective.
verses.13: When they realized that their plan had failed, they became angry and rushed towards Crete.
verses.14: But a stormy wind called Eurakylon brought rain upon her.
verses.15: Being carried away by the ship, and unable to close their eyes due to the wind, we were forced to be carried along.
verses.16: We then played some kind of role, which we called “Khauda”. We only acted in this way when the ship was about to be captured.
verses.17: So, they used their help to pull the ship out of the water. They were afraid that they might not be able to get to Syria, so they tried to move the ship along.
verses.18: But when we were severely punished for our actions, it became clear what would happen to us.
verses.19: And with the third ship, they also destroyed its equipment.
verses.20: Neither during the months of July nor during the days when the stars were visible, did winter come any closer. But hope still remained, hoping that we would be saved.
verses.21: In the midst of all these disputes, Paul remained calm and said, “Gentlemen, it is necessary for you to persuade me not to leave Crete. Only in that way can I avoid this oppression and punishment.”
verses.22: And I urge you to be courageous for now. For there will be no harm to your soul, except for the loss of your ship.
verses.23: For that night, I was present with this angel of the Lord, whom I adore.
verses.24: Say, “Do not fear, Lord Paulus. The Emperor will appear before you. And may the God be merciful to all those who are alive.”
verses.25: Therefore, be diligent, men! I believe in God that it will be so as long as you act in such a manner.
verses.26: We must go to some island.
verses.27: And on the fourteenth night, there were differences among us in Adria. In the middle of that night, the sailors said they would bring them some land to live on.
verses.28: And after spinning them several times, they found twenty ounces of gold. But when they spun them again, they found fifteen ounces of gold.
verses.29: Fearing that we might fall from the sky in dangerous places, they tied four ropes together and declared that a day would pass before we were rescued.
verses.30: But those who wanted to escape from the ship, and who were willing to cast the ship into the sea, were told to do so as if they were trying to break free from a rope that was holding them down.
verses.31: Paul said to the centurions and the soldiers, “If they do not stay on the ship, then you will not be able to survive either.”
verses.32: Then the soldiers cut the ropes that tied the ship together, and let it fall to the ground.
verses.33: But until that day came, Paul called everyone together to share in the food. He said, “Let us expect today to be the one hundred and fourteenth day; let us act accordingly, without hiring anyone.”
verses.34: Therefore, I ask you to accept this food as a gift from me. This is indeed meant for your salvation. No one among you will be deprived of food from their head.
verses.35: And after saying these words, he took bread and offered it to the God before everyone else. Then he began to eat.
verses.36: But once they became impatient, they also started to seek food.
verses.37: All the souls on that ship were seventy-six in total.
verses.38: After being fed, they hoisted the ship out of the water and set it down on the shore.
verses.39: And when that day came, we still hadn’t set sail. They had some kind of plan in mind regarding whether they should set sail or not.
verses.40: And they put the anchors in place, ready them for the sea. They also removed the ropes that were used to hold the ships together. Then they set the anchor into the ground with their breath.
verses.41: They fell into a place where they were completely destroyed. The mast remained intact, but the sails were damaged due to the violence.
verses.42: But the soldiers’ decision was to kill those who were tied up, so that no one could escape.
verses.43: But that centurion, wanting to kill Paul, deceived them into complicity in this plan. He ordered the strong men to swim across the river, and after taking the first ones along, he ordered the rest to be killed on the spot.
verses.44: And the rest, some were put on donkeys, while others were taken along with the ship. In this way, everyone was able to be saved and reach land.
